invariantRules.text: A benefit enrollment remains identifiable by person, plan version, election and coverage interval independently of payroll.
Changing election, dependent set, tier, waiver, suspension or coverage interval appends a successor state and preserves history.
Enrollment requires a plan version and may reference Employment, but may outlive active employment under continuation rules.
Election and coverage are enrollment-owned components; neither is eligibility nor a claim.
Coverage may remain active when pay is zero, no deduction exists or no payroll period exists.
A deduction on a payslip is not evidence of coverage.
Enrollment interval, coverage interval, payroll period and payment date are distinct.
Dependent coverage and tier are explicit states with source authority and effective time.
Valuation, claim adjudication and payment remain external masters.
Ending Employment does not silently end enrollment; an authorized rule or successor state is required.
Missing enrollment or coverage data is unknown, never waived or inactive by inference.
Historic enrollment remains resolvable after plan succession or retirement.
Coverage FTE is independent of the FTE used for pay comparison or proration and has its own source authority.
The payroll engine may consume an enrollment snapshot; enrollment never depends on or derives authority from a payroll result.
